# V21 IDL / V22 Python single-precision numerical equivalence

Date 2026-10-11/12.  Question: can V22 Python reproduce the original V21 IDL
lookup tables with the same original Intel single-precision DISORT binary, the
same 60 streams, the same 1000 phase-function moments and the same physical
inputs?  V21 IDL is the reference regardless of the physical accuracy of
individual DISORT results; nothing here improves the radiative transfer.

**Answer: yes.**  The three standard Terra MODIS products generated by the
corrected V22 Python release (`releases/lut_v22_single-r2.release`) are
**byte-identical to the production V21 IDL LUTs in all 52 variables** of each
file - dimensions, coordinate grids, channel identifiers, optical properties,
F0 and all nine radiative-transfer operators, including every V21 negative
value (e.g. 30 563 negative R_0v elements in pold, 36 685 in pagg).  The only
difference is the provenance attributes the release launcher adds.  Validated
on the way: the DISORT interface, viewing geometry and phase-moment arithmetic
(sections 2-5), complete DISORT-input equivalence (90/90 calls bitwise in
every argument and output), the four compact LUTs, and the full-grid
scattering properties.  A first complete run (revision 1) left two IDL
behaviours unreproduced (51/52 variables for pold and p240); both were
identified against the V21 products and corrected (section 10).

## Summary

1. **DISORT.**  The original V21 Intel DLM `DISORTtoIDL.so` is now the
   single-precision backend of the production generator, called unmodified
   with IDL's array memory layout (8 bytes past a 16-byte boundary, checked at
   run time).  It reproduces all 90 captured V21 IDL calls bitwise.
2. **UMU.**  IDL's `cos(x*!dtor)` (FLOAT product with FLOAT `!DTOR`, glibc
   `cosf`) replaces NumPy's cosine; UMU and both UMU0 values are bitwise in all
   90 calls.
3. **PMOM.**  The phase-moment differences did **not** come from the Mie
   kernel.  The first differing quantities are the Gauss-Legendre nodes and
   weights (IDL `quadrature.pro` Newton iteration vs `numpy.leggauss`); then
   the radius lattice (IDL FLOAT literal 0.001), the size parameters (FLOAT
   `wn = 1.0/wl`) and single-precision storage (IDL FLTARR at every stage).
   Correcting these, together with the refractive-index INTERPOL, makes the
   scattering file bitwise in all compact cases.  The original IDL Mie DLM and
   the gfortran build give bitwise-identical scattering properties on the full
   grids, so the Mie kernel was left unchanged.
4. **DISORT inputs.**  DTAUC, SSALB, PMOM, UTAU, UMU, PHI, UMU0, FBEAM, FISOT,
   TEMPER, WVNMLO, WVNMHI and every integer, logical and dimension argument are
   bitwise in all 90 calls; all 90 solver calls are bitwise in every output.
   The last UTAU difference was DISORT changing UTAU in place, which reaches
   the IDL caller through the DLM.
5. **Compact LUTs.**  All four compact LUTs equal the V21 IDL compact LUTs
   byte for byte in every variable (coordinates, F0, volume, all nine RT
   operators including the V21 negative values: 5 in case B, 8 in case C),
   except four optical-property variables that IDL leaves as NetCDF fill in a
   single-channel LUT (section 8).
6. **Full grids.**  For pold, p240 and pagg (36 channels, all radii) the
   extinction coefficient, its ratio, single-scatter albedo and asymmetry
   parameter, F0 (26 solar channels) and the central wavelengths and
   wavenumbers equal the production V21 LUTs bitwise.

## 2. Intel DISORT interface (`oraclut.radiative_transfer.legacy_disort`)

Selected by `ORAC_LUT_DISORT_PRECISION=single` and
`ORAC_LUT_DISORT_SP_KERNEL=intel_dlm` (the default for single precision;
`gfortran` keeps the previous kernel; double precision is unchanged).

* The Fortran entry `disort_` of the DLM is called directly with the 44
  arguments of `DISORTwrapper.c`: float32 REAL arrays and scalars, int32
  INTEGER and LOGICAL (0/1), PMOM(0:NMOM, NLYR) and UU(NUMU, NTAU, NPHI) in
  Fortran order, MAX* equal to the actual sizes, the setup_disort constants,
  TEMPER(0:NLYR).  The DLM is opened with lazy binding (its IDL_* imports are
  never used).
* Every array, outputs included, is a fresh copy placed IDL_OFFSET = 8 bytes
  past an IDL_ALIGNMENT = 16-byte boundary (`idl_placed`, asserted).  Scalars
  are fresh variables per call (DISORT's first-call self-test overwrites
  scalar arguments).
* In-place changes are returned to the caller as through the DLM: SSALB = 1
  becomes 1 - DITHER and UTAU within 1e-4 of the column optical depth is set
  to TAUC(NLYR) (`DISORTfunctions.f:681, 5262-5264`).  `call_disort` copies the
  layer arrays exactly where `call_disort.pro` does, so SSALB never reaches
  the generator while UTAU does.
* GETMOM and PLKAVG come from the same DLM.  GETMOM is identical in both
  kernels; PLKAVG differs by 1 ulp at 2000-2100 cm-1 between the Intel and
  gfortran builds.
* The Intel run time is loaded from an explicit directory (RTLD_GLOBAL;
  libifport uses libifcore symbols without declaring it), and the mapped
  libraries are checked to come from that directory.

Verification (`tests/test_v21_single_reproduction.py`): all 90 captured IDL
calls bitwise in every output array; repeated and interleaved calls with
changing layer counts; diffuse, direct-beam and emission calls; in-place
semantics against IDL's own captures; the gfortran backend still selectable.
Without the Intel module loaded and with it: identical.

## 3. Memory alignment

The ifort -O3 kernel peels a number of vectorised-loop elements that depends
on the alignment of UMU, which changes summation order in the direct-beam
intensities.  Calls bitwise against IDL by array offset modulo 64:

| offset | 0 | 4 | 8 | 12 | 24 | 40 | 56 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bitwise calls | 45 | 45 | **90** | 45 | **90** | **90** | **90** |

So the requirement is exactly "8 modulo 16", which the allocator enforces and
checks.

## 4. Viewing geometry

IDL: `UMu[0:saz_n-1] = -1.0*cos(tmpSat*!dtor)`, `UMu0 = cos(50.0*!dtor)`,
`umu0 = cos(tmpsol*!dtor)`.  `!DTOR` is FLOAT 0.017453292 (0x3C8EFA35); the
product is FLOAT and IDL's COS calls glibc `cosf` (`libidl.so` imports it).
`oraclut.idl_math.idl_cos_deg` reproduces this; used at the six sites of
`create_orac_luts.py`.

| | NumPy (before) | IDL arithmetic |
|---|---|---|
| UMU arrays (90 calls; satellite zeniths 0-65 deg incl. nadir rule and instrument maximum) | 90 differ (1 ulp) | 90/90 bitwise |
| nominal UMU0 = cos 50 deg (45 diffuse/emission calls) | 45 differ | 45/45 bitwise |
| direct-beam UMU0 (45 calls) | bitwise | bitwise |

The grid, its ordering and the |UMU| = 1 -> 0.99999 rule are unchanged.  On
every production angle glibc `cosf` equals the correctly rounded cosine.

## 5. Phase-moment arithmetic

A diagnostic replica of the IDL chain (`v21_v22_single/scattering_replica.py`)
reproduces the IDL `scatfile.sav` (bext550, w550, g550, phs550, amom550,
bextrat, bext, w, g, phs, amom) bitwise in all four compact cases, and with
the uncorrected options reproduces the 17de4c0 Python scatfile bitwise.  Its
intermediates are therefore those of the IDL computation (inferred: only the
final scatfile was captured inside IDL).

Stage trace at the failing p240 node (case A, channel 6, r_e = 29 um;
`results/stage4_trace_A_r1.json`), uncorrected Python vs IDL:

| Stage | Type | Shape | Bitwise | Differing | Max abs | Max ulp | Responsible operation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| refractive index (0.55 um, channel) | complex64 | scalar | yes | 0 | 0 | 0 | |
| **phase-function cosines QV** | float64 | 1000 | **no (first)** | 47 | 1.1e-16 | 2 | quadrature.pro Newton nodes vs leggauss |
| Gauss-Legendre weights | float64 | 1000 | no | 1000 | 6.7e-14 | 7.9e7 | as above |
| Npts | int | | yes | | | | |
| radius abscissae R | float64 | 2855 / 964 | no | all | 4.8e-11 | 2.2e8 | Rl = DOUBLE(FLOAT 0.001) |
| size distribution W1P | float64 | | no | all | 1.4e-10 | 1.3e10 | R, FLOAT S |
| size parameters Dx | float64 | | no | all | 4.1e-5 | 6.3e8 | FLOAT wn = 1.0/wl |
| Mie Qext, F11 | float64 | | no | all | F11 13.2 (0.55 um) | | different Dx (Mie resonances) |
| Bext, w, g, SPM (DOUBLE) | float64 | | no | | | | propagated |
| Bext550 (FLOAT) | float32 | | no | 1 | 4.9e-4 | 2 | |
| Bext, w, g (FLOAT) | float32 | | yes | 0 | | | |
| BextRat (FLOAT/FLOAT) | float32 | | no | 1 | 1.2e-7 | 1 | double division vs FLOAT/FLOAT |
| Phs550, Phs (FLOAT) | float32 | 1000 | no | 991, 748 | 7.8e-3 | 1217, 39 | |
| AMom550, AMom (FLOAT) | float32 | 1000 | no | 880, 819 | 3.0e-8 | (sign changes near 0) | legpexp of DOUBLE vs FLOAT Phs |
| Mie kernels, identical inputs (gfortran vs Intel) | float64 | | no | | Q 1.7e-14, F11 1.9e-10 | Q 38 | build differences, absorbed by float32 storage |

One-at-a-time ablation (`results/scattering_ablation.json`; scatfile elements
differing from IDL when one option is switched back to the old arithmetic,
cases A/B/C/D): FLOAT wavenumber 10208/9031/10177/10867; FLTARR storage
3925/3581/4502/4565; IDL quadrature 2903/3578/3788/4249; FLOAT literals
2229/3524/2983/3798; refractive-index INTERPOL 0/1617/0/0; trapezium formula,
W1P evaluation order, glibc exp/pow, Mie kernel and Mie memory layout 0.

Corrections in production (all mirror an IDL expression, quoted in comments):

* `create_bwgp`: quadrature.pro 'G' Newton iteration and 'T' formula; FLOAT
  `wn = 1.0/wl`; `[Rm, S, 0.001, 100.0]` promoted from FLOAT; `xres` FLOAT
  0.4; `W1*(Nd/n)*R^alpha*exp(-b*R)` with glibc pow/exp; `((W1PA*4.)/3.)*R`;
  FLTARR Bext, w, g, Phi.
* `generate_scattering_properties`: IDL INTERPOL of the COMPLEX refractive
  index (`load_mmdat`: `complex(n, -k)` single precision); FLTARR component and
  class arrays (legpexp expands the FLOAT phase function; BextRat FLOAT/FLOAT);
  Baum phase angles `acos(QV)*180./!pi` (glibc acos, FLOAT !pi).
* `baum`: FLOAT tables, FLOAT INTERPOL indices, FLOAT radius extrapolation,
  INTERPOLATE evaluated in double: reproduces the production V21 pagg optical
  properties bitwise (3 x 864 values), where float32 interpolation or double
  indices do not (71-313 differ; `results/baum_interpolate.json`).  For the
  phase function IDL also converts the DOUBLE phase-angle index to FLOAT
  (INTERPOLATE locations are FLOAT; found from the revision-1 products,
  section 10).
* FLOAT `EXP` (Rayleigh profile, T_dv direct-beam term) is the DOUBLE glibc
  `exp` rounded to FLOAT, not `expf` (section 10).

## 6. Complete DISORT inputs

`v21_v22_single/compare_inputs.py corrected` (arguments recorded at the entry
of the Intel backend; `results/corrected/compare_inputs.json`): every array and
scalar argument and every integer, logical and dimension argument bitwise in
all 90 calls.  The Rayleigh layers needed IDL's integer power
(`wvl_centre^4 = (w*w)*(w*w)`; NumPy's powf form differed in cases A-C) and the
FLOAT `exp` of glibc.  UTAU differed in 15 direct-beam calls until DISORT's
in-place change of UTAU was propagated (section 2).

## 7. Solver outputs

90/90 calls bitwise in RFLDIR, RFLDN, FLUP, DFDT, UAVG, UU, ALBMED and TRNMED.

## 8. Compact LUTs

`v21_v22_single/compare_compact_luts.py corrected`, against the V21 IDL
compact LUTs of `idl_double/results/run_20261010T214143` (equal to the
production V21 products in every RT coefficient):

| Case | Variables | Raw-byte identical | Not identical |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (ch6, tau 64-256, r_e 27-31, SZA 70/80) | 37 | 33 | 4 single-channel optical properties |
| B (ch20, mixed) | 52 | 48 | same 4 |
| C (ch6, tau 0.0625-0.25) | 37 | 33 | same 4 |
| D (ch1) | 37 | 33 | same 4 |

Negative V21 values reproduced exactly (B: 5, C: 8).  The four variables
`extinction_coefficient`, `extinction_coefficient_ratio`,
`single_scatter_albedo` and `asymmetry_parameter` are all NetCDF fill in the
IDL compact files: with one channel, `reform(Bext[m,*,*])` drops the channel
dimension and IDL's `NCDF_VARPUT` writes nothing (no message in the IDL log).
The multi-channel production V21 LUTs contain the values, and V22 writes the
values (bitwise equal to the IDL scatfile).  This write artefact of
single-channel IDL runs is not emulated.

Post-processing corrections needed for the compact LUTs: the writer divides by
100 (IDL `TD/100`), RFD/TFD use `100.*FlUp[0]/(FIsot*!pi)`, EM accumulates
`100.0*UU/BBE`, TD uses FLOAT `exp`, and F0 follows the IDL types (DOUBLE solar
spectrum, IDL INTERPOL; `loadxyz` reads DOUBLE).

## 9. Representative cases

* Full-grid scattering (`v21_v22_single/full_grid_scattering.py`;
  `results/full_grid/`): pold and p240 (36 channels x 20 radii) and pagg
  (36 x 24) - extinction coefficient, ratio, albedo, asymmetry bitwise
  against the production V21 LUTs.  Solar, mixed and thermal channels, small
  and large radii.
* The original IDL Mie DLM (called through a development backend that was not
  retained) and the gfortran build give bitwise-identical scatfiles on the full
  pold and p240 grids, including all 720 000 phase-function values and moments
  each (`results/full_grid/mie_kernels_scatfile.json`).
* F0: bitwise for all 26 solar channels in all three products; central
  wavelengths and wavenumbers 36/36.
* DISORT-level evidence beyond the compact cases (other optical depths, the
  SZA 80 support nodes of all products, pold and pagg phase functions) comes
  from the complete LUTs (section 10).  No additional IDL captures were needed.

## 10. Complete V21/V22 LUT comparison

**Revision 1** (`releases/lut_v22_single.release`, jobs 495402-495404, run
2026-10-11 23:10 to 2026-10-12 03:50, 4 h 32 min to 4 h 40 min each; products
kept in `staging/lut_v22_single/`; `v21_v22_single/results/full_luts_r1/`).
A first submission (495399-495401) had been cancelled after 15 minutes because
the first form of that manifest (`d38af77`, sha256 `4b448419...`) used a role
launcher v03 cannot parse; it was rewritten (same files and hashes) before any
product was made.

| Product | Variables raw-byte identical | Differing |
|---|---|---|
| pold | 51/52 | T_dv: 37 of 122 400 elements (up to 82 ulp; cancellation) |
| p240 | 51/52 | T_dv: 46 of 122 400 |
| pagg | 44/52 | all eight solar/thermal RT operators, ~90 % of elements, p99 3e-5 to 9e-5 absolute (max 0.015 in R_0v) |

Dimensions, coordinates, channel identifiers, attributes, F0, volume and the
optical properties were identical in all three products.  Diagnosis by
controlled reruns of single channels on the full grids against the V21
products (scratch experiments, production code otherwise unchanged):

| Experiment | Differing from V21 |
|---|---|
| pold channel 7 T_dv, glibc `expf` (revision 1) | 2 of 3 400 |
| pold channel 7 T_dv, DOUBLE `exp` rounded to FLOAT | **0** |
| pold channel 7 T_dv, NumPy float32 `exp` | 615 |
| pagg channel 1, Baum phase-angle index DOUBLE (revision 1) | T_dv 3781/4080, R_0v 419 413/448 800, ... |
| pagg channel 1, float32 interpolation arithmetic | T_dv 3295/4080, ... |
| pagg channel 1, phase-angle index converted to FLOAT, double arithmetic | T_dv 3/4080 (the `exp` effect), all other operators **0** |

T_dv = UU - 100 exp(totaltau/UMU) cancels strongly, so a 1-ulp difference of
the exponential appears as up to 82 ulp of T_dv.  Revision 2 (`c591d2b`:
`idl_math` v02, `baum` v03) uses the rounded DOUBLE `exp` and FLOAT
INTERPOLATE locations; with it the two experiments give 0 differences in every
operator (pold channel 7 T_dv; pagg channel 1, all eight operators), and the
compact cases remain bitwise (90/90 DISORT calls, all compact LUT variables).

**Revision 2** (`releases/lut_v22_single-r2.release`, sha256 `33c7f64c...`,
commit `c591d2b`; jobs 495405-495407, run 2026-10-12 06:21 to 10:58, 4 h 31
min to 4 h 37 min each on atmnode009; products in
`staging/lut_v22_single-r2/`; `v21_v22_single/compare_full_luts.py`,
`results/full_luts/`):

| Product | Variables raw-byte identical to V21 | Decoded values differing | Negative values V21 / V22 (R_0v, T_dv, E_md) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `terra_modis_m_liquid-water_a01_pold_v22.nc` | **52/52** | 0 | 30 563 / 30 563, 901 / 901, 944 / 944 |
| `terra_modis_m_liquid-water_a01_p240_v22.nc` | **52/52** | 0 | 30 585 / 30 585, 971 / 971, 953 / 953 |
| `terra_modis_m_water-ice_a01_pagg_v22.nc` | **52/52** | 0 | 36 685 / 36 685, 2366 / 2366, 1152 / 1152 |

Identical dimensions (names and lengths), variable order, coordinate grids,
channel identifiers, variable attributes, storage types (float32, no
packing).  Global attributes: V21 has none that V22 lacks; V22 adds
`lut_release`, `lut_release_version` and the `provenance_*` attributes of the
release launcher.  All maximum, RMS, p95 and p99 differences are zero, and
the historical V21 DISORT failures (sections of the SZA 80 direct-beam calls,
negative reflectances and transmissions) are reproduced exactly.

## 11. Forward-model and Jacobian comparisons

Every RT operator, coordinate and optical property of the three products is
raw-byte identical to V21, so ORAC's interpolated coefficients, reconstructed
radiances and retrieval Jacobians are identical everywhere - inside the
operational domain (SZA, VZA < 75 deg) and through the SZA 80 support nodes
alike.  No separate forward-model evaluation is needed;
`compare_full_luts.py` records this in `results/full_luts/<product>.json`
(it would otherwise run the `operational_domain.py` analysis).

## 15. Remaining discrepancies and next steps

* Single-channel IDL LUTs leave four optical-property variables as fill
  (section 8); not emulated.
* The Baum phase-function interpolation (FLOAT locations, double
  arithmetic) is verified by the revision-2 pagg product (bitwise).
* Paths not exercised against IDL here: log-normal (aerosol) size
  distributions still use NumPy exp/log; `read_baum_channel`; aerosol LUTs.
  The corrected arithmetic applies to every precision and formulation; the
  sealed double-precision release is unaffected (it runs its own sources).
* Owner decisions: create the `lut-code-v22.4` tag; whether and how to promote
  the revision-2 products (staged only; the shared ORAC LUT directory is
  untouched); whether to keep or remove the revision-1 products in
  `staging/lut_v22_single/`.
